candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement / CMS HAC-POA payment provision
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish the CMS HAC Present-on-Admission payment provision from the separate HAC Reduction Program and recognize the payment implication of a selected HAC that was not present on admission.

options.A: The hospital does not receive additional payment attributable to the selected HAC; the case is paid as though that secondary diagnosis were not present
options.B: Every occurrence automatically causes a 1% reduction in all Medicare payments to the hospital for the year
options.C: The hospital receives a higher DRG payment because the new pressure injury increases case severity
options.D: The condition is excluded from HAC policy because pressure injuries are not on the CMS HAC list

candidate.rationale: CMS states that for selected Hospital-Acquired Conditions that were not present on admission, the hospital does not receive additional payment attributable to that condition; the case is paid as though the secondary diagnosis were not present. Stage III and IV pressure ulcers are included on the HAC list. This HAC Present-on-Admission payment provision is separate from the HAC Reduction Program, which can reduce payments by 1% for hospitals in the worst-performing quartile on selected HAC measures. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For a selected HAC such as a Stage III/IV pressure ulcer that was not present on admission, the HAC POA payment provision prevents additional payment attributable to that secondary diagnosis.
candidate.source_document_title: Hospital-Acquired Conditions — Present on Admission Indicator and HAC Payment Provision
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'Present on Admission Indicator' and 'HAC Payment Provision': selected conditions are high cost/high volume, result in higher DRG payment as secondary diagnoses, and could reasonably have been prevented; for selected HACs not present on admission, hospitals do not receive additional payment and the case is paid as though the secondary diagnosis were not present; HAC list includes Stage III and IV Pressure Ulcers
candidate.stem: A hospital quality team reviews a Medicare IPPS case in which a Stage III pressure injury developed during the hospitalization and was not present on admission. Which CMS payment principle applies under the Hospital-Acquired Conditions Present-on-Admission payment provision?
